title: How Dog Shows Work
summary: Josh and Chuck explain how dog shows work, focusing on AKC conformation shows and the Westminster Kennel Club Dog Show at Madison Square Garden. They open with a plug for the Science Channel TV show, then describe how dogs are judged against breed standards (attitude, balance, head, teeth, coat, color), how champion points and majors are earned at specialty shows through winners dog/bitch, best of breed, and group placements, and how Best in Show is chosen from seven groups. They cover the AKC breed groups, criticism of purebred breeding (inherited defects, shorter lives, eugenics comparisons, tail docking and ear cropping), England's Crufts including its Scruffs event for crossbreeds, agility and obedience trials, and some dog show records. The episode ends with listener mail about a woman crying at the musical Wicked, and a sign-off.
topics: Stuff You Should Know TV show

segments.title: Opening banter and TV show plug
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck plug their Science Channel TV show premiering at 10 pm, with episodes sold on iTunes for $1.99, then introduce the topic of dog shows and their own interest in watching them.
topics: Stuff You Should Know TV show

segments.title: How dogs are judged against breed standards
segments.summary: Conformation shows judge purebred dogs against AKC breed standards covering attitude, gait, balance, head, eyes, ears, teeth, coat, and color. The dog closest to the idealized breed standard wins.

segments.title: Westminster history and earning a championship
segments.summary: Westminster has been held at Madison Square Garden since 1877 and has awarded Best in Show since 1907. Dogs become champions by earning 15 points from three judges or two majors from separate judges, mainly at specialty shows.

segments.title: Specialty show classes and winners
segments.summary: Specialty shows divide dogs by sex into classes such as puppy, novice, bred by exhibitor, American bred, and open. First-place winners compete for winners dog and winners bitch, then best of breed, best of opposite sex, and points are awarded up to five.

segments.title: AKC breed groups and Best in Show selection
segments.summary: The AKC recognizes a little over 100 breeds in seven groups: sporting, hound, working, terrier, toy, non-sporting, and herding, plus a miscellaneous class for breeds seeking recognition. Best of breed winners compete in groups, and group winners go to the all-breed Best in Show judging.

segments.title: Criticism of purebred breeding
segments.summary: Critics say purebred breeding narrows the gene pool and causes shorter lives, disease, and defects such as Dalmatian deafness/blindness and German shepherd hip dysplasia. Joanna Goldberg compares breeding to eugenics. The AKC recognized a breed petitioned by the American Border Collie Association, and tail docking and ear cropping are objected to.

segments.title: Crufts, Scruffs, agility and obedience
segments.summary: England's Kennel Club runs Crufts, which includes agility and obedience and is criticized for moving away from conformation. Its Scruffs event welcomes crossbreed dogs judged on temperament, health, and character. Agility involves off-leash obstacle courses and obedience involves handler commands, with the National Obedience Champion title.

segments.title: Dog show records and trivia
segments.summary: The Fox Terrier has won Best in Show the most times, with 13 wins. Champion Warren Remedy won three times in a row in the early 1900s. The oldest winner was an eight-year-old Papillon, and the youngest was a Rough Collie about nine months old.

segments.title: Listener mail: crying during Wicked
segments.summary: Angela from Columbus, Ohio, shares how she sobbed during the Defying Gravity song at a touring production of Wicked. The hosts then invite dog show stories and give contact details.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck wish listeners a happy new year, give their Twitter handle and Facebook page, and point to the website for more on dog shows.
